questions.stem: 79M, EVAR 5y ago, sac re-expansion to 8.4cm: management, imaging, endo & open options
questions.verbatim: A 79 year old male had undergone EVAR for treatment of 6.3cm dia infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm 5 y previously. Type II diabetic 17 yr. CABG 9y previously. BMI 32. 45 pack year smoking history. After initial sac size reduction to 5.4cm dia by 3.5yrs post EVAR, sac measurement on duplex ultrasound performed 2 weeks ago in a general radiology practice is reported at “8.4cm”. a) Discuss your initial management of this patient. b) Compare and contrast the modalities to image the aortic aneurysm which you might reasonably utilize as you assess this patient. c) Discuss endovascular interventional treatment strategies for this man and provide a rationale for each. d) Elaborate on the circumstances and techniques of open operative interventions which might reasonably be considered.

questions.stem: Causes of B-mode ultrasound artefacts and mitigation
questions.verbatim: Ultrasound artefact: Describe the causes of ultrasound artefacts and give one example of how an artefact occurs in B mode ultrasound and how to mitigate that artefact.

questions.stem: 48F digital ulceration, cold-induced colour change (Raynaud's)
questions.verbatim: Discuss your management of a 48 year female who presents with digital ulceration to her left index and middle finger. She has noted intermittent colour changes to the hands, more so the left hand and especially in the cooler months of the year.

questions.stem: Diagnosis of osteomyelitis in a diabetic foot ulcer
questions.verbatim: Compare and contrast the modalities and methods of diagnosis of osteomyelitis in a diabetic foot ulcer.

questions.stem: Perioperative management of NOAC (dabigatran/rivaroxaban)
questions.verbatim: How would you manage a patient you are preparing for surgery who is on a new oral anticoagulant, such as dabigitran or rivaroxaban.

questions.stem: 69M 66mm AAA + CIA, smoker/COPD: open vs EVAR, post-procedural care
questions.verbatim: A 69 year old male presents with a 66mm AAA. The aneurysm involves one CIA (to iliac bifurcation) and has a 4mm length neck. He is a smoker and has moderate COPD (FEV1 1.6L). 1) How would you advise him about the requirement for intervention and what further assessment or treatment would you give him prior to any intervention? 2) Compare and contrast open vs Endovascular Repair (2 sections). 3) What post-procedural management would you give?

questions.stem: Risk factors for iodinated contrast reactions & mitigation
questions.verbatim: Describe and discuss risk factors for iodinated contrast adverse reactions in angiography and measures you might take to mitigate those risks.

questions.stem: Blunt knee trauma, tibial plateau #, posterior knee dislocation: assess circulation
questions.verbatim: Describe your assessment and initial management plan for a patient you are called to see in A&E with a history of blunt trauma to the knee, a fracture of the tibial plateau and posterior dislocation of the knee. You may assume that this is an isolated injury and you are asked to assess the circulation.

questions.stem: Type II endoleak after EVAR: indications & treatment
questions.verbatim: Discuss the indications for and treatment options for a Type 2 endoleak after EVAR.

questions.stem: 17F palmar hyperhidrosis 8 years
questions.verbatim: Discuss the management of a 17 year old female who presents with sweaty palms for the last 8 years.

questions.stem: 65M claudication, 10cm SFA occlusion; stent occlusion/ALI; AF antiplatelet/anticoag
questions.verbatim: A 65 year old man presents with a 6 month history of 100-200 m claudication. Imaging suggests a 10cm Occlusion of the mid to distal Superficial Femoral Artery. 1) Discuss how you would further assess him. 2) What factors would you take into account in advising him to consider: a) endovascular intervention b) femoro-popliteal bypass or c) non-interventional management. Take the point of view of a patient wanting to know the options. 3) He subsequently goes on to have angioplasty and stenting of the SFA and now presents at 9 months with a stent occlusion (now a 15cm Occlusion). He has sudden onset of new claudication and a cold foot. Describe how you would manage this. 4) He has successful endovascular intervention. It was thought he had in-stent re-stenosis. He is also now in atrial fibrillation. Describe how you would manage his anti-coagulation and anti-platelet therapy. He is asking about how you would balance the risks and benefits of each agent either singly or in combination.

questions.stem: Graft surveillance ultrasound: stenosis criteria, evidence
questions.verbatim: Ultrasound imaging is commonly used for femorodistal graft surveillance. Discuss the utility of graft surveillance and describe how you interpret findings on a graft scan including criteria for defining graft stenosis, indications for intervention and evidence for improved graft patency.

questions.stem: Fibromuscular dysplasia of renal arteries in new hypertension
questions.verbatim: Discuss implications of finding fibromuscular dysplasia affecting renal arteries during investigation of new onset hypertension in a middle aged woman and how you would investigate further.

questions.stem: Renal artery rupture during cardiology renal stenting - plan
questions.verbatim: While consulting in your rooms you are called by a scout nurse in the cath lab because a cardiology colleague while placing a renal stent has ruptured the renal artery. What is your plan of action?

questions.stem: 60yo diabetic for haemodialysis: compare access options
questions.verbatim: Discuss your assessment of a 60 year old diabetic who is referred to you by a renal physician for haemodialysis. Compare and contrast the surgical options for haemodialysis access.

questions.stem: 45M obese diabetic, infected plantar ulcer at 1st MTPJ, no pedal pulses; debridement & revascularisation
questions.verbatim: A 45yr old obese diabetic male presents to the A&E Department of your hospital with an infected plantar ulcer related to his left 1st Metatarsophalangeal joint. His BP is 150/95, PR 110, temp 38.70 Celsius, and with a blood sugar level of 20mmol/L. The pedal pulses are not palpable. 1) Outline your assessment and management prior to any operative intervention. 2) A local debridement is planned that evening. Discuss the principles of this and your post-operative management? 3) Discuss your assessment of the requirement for, timing and type of revascularisation that maybe needed. 4) Discuss the long term management of this patients foot/feet.

questions.stem: 74M amaurosis fugax, prior neck radiotherapy (SCC), >70% L ICA stenosis: treatment options
questions.verbatim: A 74 year old man presents with recent onset of daily episodes of amaurosis fugax affecting his left eye. Significant past history includes prior left sided neck surgery and radiotherapy for an SCC 10 years ago. Ultrasound shows evidence of a critical stenosis of greater than 70% in the left ICA. Compare treatment options available and explain how different factors would be important in your decision making.

questions.stem: 20F AVM of thigh diagnosed in childhood, concerns re pregnancy: evaluation & advice
questions.verbatim: A 20 year old female presents with a swelling on the left antero-lateral thigh. She says that she was diagnosed with a vascular malformation as a child. She is concerned about what might happen in a pregnancy. How would you evaluate the lesion and what advice would you give?

questions.stem: Publication of performance / league tables for procedures such as CEA: arguments
questions.verbatim: Discuss the publication of performance / league tables for procedures such as carotid endarterectomy and give your reasons for supporting or opposing them.

questions.stem: GP advice on management of superficial vein thrombosis in the leg
questions.verbatim: Describe the advice you would provide a General Practitioner who telephones seeking management guidance for a patient with an ultrasound which reports superficial vein thrombosis in a leg.

questions.stem: 30yo triathlete ischaemic foot, popliteal cystic adventitial disease; fasciotomy, foot drop
questions.verbatim: A male, 30yr old tri athlete presents with an ischaemic left foot to the Accident and Emergency department. He remarks over the last 9 months his average cycle and running times have reduced. His BP is 170/70, PR 55, temp 36.7 Celsius. The only other findings are that the left popliteal and pedal pulses are not palpable. 1a) Outline your assessment and management prior to any operative intervention with particular reference to a potential differential diagnosis. 1b) You receive a phone call from the A&E consultant 2 hours following presentation stating that the patient has now developed an insensate foot with difficulty in moving the foot. He has a CT with contrast scan that demonstrates pathology in his popliteal artery. Discuss your management of this patient with this new information at hand? 1c) He goes onto have an emergency femoro popliteal bypass graft for an occluded popliteal artery secondary to popliteal cystic adventitial disease. Four compartment calf fasciotomies were performed with skin incisions closed primarily medially and with skin grafting laterally. On discharge there is a residual foot drop. Discuss the long term management of this patient. 1d) Two years post-operatively the patient represents with symptoms of claudication in the operated leg. Discuss and compare management options.

questions.stem: 21F axillo-subclavian vein occlusion (Paget-Schroetter)
questions.verbatim: A 21 year old female attends with right arm swelling present for 6 days. An ultrasound shows occlusion of the right axillary/subclavian vein. The patient is very anxious and wants to know what options she has. 2a) How would you assess her for treatment? 2b) Compare and contrast the short and long term outcomes of the various modes of treatment?

questions.stem: Spinal cord ischaemia after thoraco-abdominal aortic repair: risk & protection
questions.verbatim: Paraplegia remains a devastating complication following thoracic aortic repair. 3a) What are the risk factors for spinal cord ischaemia following repair of the thoraco-abdominal aorta? 3b) Appraise techniques that are available to reduce spinal ischaemic complications.

questions.stem: >60% renal artery stenosis with hypertension: management
questions.verbatim: You are referred a patient with hypertension and possible renal artery stenosis. An arterial duplex scan suggests a greater than 60% renal artery stenosis. How would you manage this patient?

questions.stem: 59F lower-extremity swelling: assessment & treatment
questions.verbatim: A 59 year old female is referred to you by her GP with lower extremity swelling. Discuss assessment of the patient and evaluate treatment options.

questions.stem: 54F gaiter venous ulcer, GSV/SSV incompetence & perforators; recurrence; deep reflux
questions.verbatim: A 54 year old woman presents with a large ulcer in the gaiter area of her left leg of 2 years duration. Her background history includes malignant hyperthermia diagnosed following a tooth extraction 10 years ago. Her venous ultrasound scan shows the following: Incompetent sapheno-femoral and sapheno-popliteal junctions. Incompetence of the entire length of the great saphenous vein. Incompetence of the short saphenous vein down to the mid calf. Three incompetent perforators at 2cm, 5cm and 7cm proximal to the ankle joint communicating with the great saphenous vein. 1a) Discuss the assessment of this patient. 1b) How would you manage the ulcer and the underlying venous reflux? 1c) Two years post treatment, she re-presents with a recurrent ulcer. Repeat ultrasound shows reflux at the sapheno-femoral junction into a recurrent/residual vein to the level of the mid thigh. There are still 3 incompetent calf perforators. Discuss your plan of management. 1d) Evaluate the role and methods of treating superficial venous disease in a patient with significant reflux in the deep veins.

questions.stem: Causes, evaluation & management of stroke after carotid endarterectomy
questions.verbatim: 2a) Discuss the causes of stroke following carotid endarterectomy? 2b) How would you evaluate and manage a patient who develops a stroke following carotid endarterectomy? (In the perioperative period)

questions.stem: 36F infected forearm PTFE loop fistula
questions.verbatim: The renal physicians ask you to review and treat a 36 year old female with a likely infected (L) forearm PTFE loop fistula. 3a) Outline your assessment and management strategy.

questions.stem: 72M occluded femoro-popliteal bypass: assess & manage
questions.verbatim: A 72-year-old male presents to emergency with occlusion of a femoro-popliteal bypass. 4a) How would you assess and manage this patient?

questions.stem: 67F with HITS needing elective vascular intervention
questions.verbatim: A 67 year old female requires vascular intervention as an elective procedure. She was diagnosed with heparin induced thrombocytopaenic syndrome (HITS) following coronary artery bypass surgery 5 years ago. 5a) Formulate a management strategy for this patient.

questions.stem: 19F blunt thoracic aortic injury + polytrauma: classification, TEVAR
questions.verbatim: A 19 year old female is an unrestrained passenger in a road traffic crash. A pan-CT reveals a traumatic thoracic aortic injury. Her other injuries include a closed head injury, a liver laceration and a femoral fracture. a) Discuss the pathophysiology of traumatic thoracic aortic injuries. Describe a classification system for traumatic thoracic aortic injuries and how it could be used to guide treatment. b) Discuss management priorities for this patient. c) What treatment strategies may be available for traumatic thoracic aortic injury? Explain under what circumstances these strategies may be used and what are the potential advantages and disadvantages of these strategies. d) Your preference is to perform a thoracic endovascular stent graft. Evaluate the potential issues associated with treating this patient and discuss strategies to prevent and manage these.

questions.stem: 65M recurrent R hemispheric TIA, occluded R ICA
questions.verbatim: A 65 year old male presents with recurrent right hemispheric transient ischaemic events and an ultrasound report of an occluded right internal carotid artery. Discuss your management of this gentleman.

questions.stem: 23F uncomplicated varicose veins (CEAP C2): options
questions.verbatim: A 23 year old female presents wanting information regarding the treatment of uncomplicated varicose veins (CEAP class 2). Discuss and compare her management options.

questions.stem: 78F acute mesenteric ischaemia (SMA), AF
questions.verbatim: You are asked by the general surgeons to review a 78 year old female who presents with sudden onset severe paraumbilical pain. She is clinically in atrial fibrillation with a heart rate of 120. You are informed that an abdominal CT performed shortly after presentation suggests pathology within the superior mesenteric artery. Discuss the management options.

questions.stem: 59F SVC obstruction from mediastinal lymphoma
questions.verbatim: A 59 year old woman presents with gradually increasing swelling of her face and both arms. She has had a diagnosis of Non-Hodgkins Lymphoma with mediastinal involvement treated with chemotherapy and radiotherapy 18 months ago. She is considered to be in remission. Discuss management options.

questions.stem: 60F renal tumour invading renal vein & IVC: thrombectomy, IVC reconstruction
questions.verbatim: You are contacted by an Urologist about a 60-year-old woman with a right renal tumour which has invaded the right renal vein and extends into the inferior vena cava (IVC). She has been planned for operative intervention and you are asked to be available to help with surgery. a) How would you evaluate this patient for surgery? b) What surgical approaches are available for thrombectomy/resection of such a tumour? How is your decision affected by the extent of caval involvement? c) Discuss the consequences of IVC resection and the principles of venous reconstruction. d) Five days following surgery, the patient develops swelling to her left leg. How would you investigate and manage this problem?

questions.stem: 69M, 70-79% ulcerated L ICA stenosis, symptomatic
questions.verbatim: A 69-year-old man presents with right arm weakness and dysphasia. Duplex ultrasound suggests a 70-79% stenosis of the left internal carotid artery origin by an ulcerated plaque. The common carotid artery waveforms demonstrate low velocities. How will you manage this patient?

questions.stem: 52F incidental 3cm hepatic artery aneurysm
questions.verbatim: Discuss the management of a 52-year-old female who presents with an incidental ultrasound finding of a 3cm aneurysm of the hepatic artery.

questions.stem: IVDU with pulsatile groin mass (mycotic femoral pseudoaneurysm)
questions.verbatim: You are asked to assess a known intravenous drug user who presents to the accident and emergency department with a tender enlarging pulsatile mass in their right groin. Outline your management.

questions.stem: Profuse bleeding after thigh tourniquet deflation post-TKR
questions.verbatim: You receive a phone call from the operating theatre of a peripheral hospital. Upon deflating a thigh tourniquet used during a knee replacement there is profuse bleeding. The tourniquet has been reinflated. What is your initial advice and subsequent management?

questions.stem: 72M mycotic/infected infrarenal aortic mass; infected endostent; graft infection
questions.verbatim: A 72 year old male presents to hospital with deep abdominal and back pains associated with fevers, malaise and weight loss over the last month. He is an avid traveller and has recently returned from an overseas holiday. A “FAST scan” performed in the A&E department suggests the presence of a 4.5 cm infrarenal aortic mass. a) Outline your assessment and initial management. What investigations would you arrange and why? b) Your investigations suggest non-malignant pathology involving the abdominal aorta. Discuss and contrast the management options. c) An endostent is placed. A CT scan performed on the third day postoperatively shows the mass has increased in size to 6 cm and there is gas in the aortic sac. The patient wants active treatment. Describe in detail your management plan. d) You had decided to treat the patient by excising the infected aorta, oversewing the aortic stump and performing a bilateral axillo-femoral bypass. They represent 3 years following the surgery with an infected right femoral anastomosis. Discuss your management options.

questions.stem: Cerebral protection & neuromonitoring during carotid endarterectomy
questions.verbatim: Discuss the options for cerebral protection and neurological monitoring during carotid endarterectomy.

questions.stem: Surgical approaches to thoracic outlet decompression
questions.verbatim: Compare and contrast the surgical approaches to thoracic outlet decompression.

questions.stem: Mechanisms of failure of endovascular therapy in femoro-popliteal disease
questions.verbatim: Explain the mechanisms of failure of endovascular therapy in femoro-popliteal occlusive disease and how these can be managed.

questions.stem: Paclitaxel-coated device meta-analysis: risk/benefit & mitigation
questions.verbatim: A recent meta-analysis of data investigating Paclitaxel coated devices used in peripheral leg vessels has identified significant evidence for concern. Briefly outline this recent evidence, and discuss the risk/benefit of continued use of these devices and possible strategies to mitigate adverse patient outcomes.

questions.stem: Perioperative infection rate quadrupled: audit/QI approach
questions.verbatim: Your audit process has revealed that your perioperative infection rate has quadrupled over the previous 6 months. You are tasked by your department to manage this development. Discuss your approach.

questions.stem: Penetrating neck injury, bleeding zone above clavicle; trauma team leadership & control
questions.verbatim: As the on-call vascular consultant and leader of the trauma team, you have been called in to the emergency department to help manage a young adult male who has been involved in an altercation outside a night club. The patient is arriving by ambulance but is still 5 minutes away. You have been informed that the patient has an obvious laceration to the left side of his neck which is bleeding heavily but have little other information. a) As the trauma team leader, describe how you would prepare for the patient’s arrival and initially manage their care. b) How would you assess a penetrating neck injury and the need for vascular intervention? c) Describe an algorithm you might use for the management of this patient based upon the outcomes of your assessment. d) The patient has a single obvious penetrating injury to the neck within the anterior triangle, 2 cm above the clavicle. He has been intubated and remains hypotensive. A nurse has her fingers pressing on the wound but blood is actively extravasating around her fingers. Describe in detail how you would establish definitive control of the patient’s bleeding.

questions.stem: 78M 6cm AAA + 3.5cm CIA: EVAR iliac management options
questions.verbatim: A 78 year old male has a 6 cm infra-renal abdominal aortic aneurysm and a 3.5 cm left common iliac aneurysm extending to the iliac bifurcation. You decide to proceed with endovascular aneurysm repair. Evaluate the options for management of the iliac arteries.

questions.stem: Role of venous intervention in venous ulceration
questions.verbatim: Evaluate the role of venous intervention in the management of venous ulceration.

questions.stem: Deep plantar ulcer & necrotic hallux in obese IDDM
questions.verbatim: Discuss your evaluation and initial management of a deep plantar-surface foot ulcer and necrotic hallux in an obese insulin-dependent diabetic.

questions.stem: Assessment & management of vascular malformations
questions.verbatim: Discuss the assessment and management of vascular malformations.

questions.stem: Patient died on table: steps to address from here
questions.verbatim: You have had a particularly challenging day in theatre and your patient admitted after a severe Motor Vehicle Accident has just died on the table. Outline the steps that need to be addressed from here.

questions.stem: 55M T2DM toe ulcer/osteomyelitis CLTI: angiosome, tibial revascularisation, failure
questions.verbatim: A 55 year old male with type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with ulceration of the tip of the left great toe with mild surrounding cellulitis. X-ray confirms osteomyelitis of the distal phalanx. Femoral and popliteal pulses are palpable. No pedal pulses are palpable. The left great toe pressure is 30 mmHg. You commence oral antibiotics and perform a diagnostic angiogram. The angiogram confirms patent superficial femoral and popliteal arteries with no evidence of stenosis. The anterior tibial artery is patent at its origin then occludes. It reconstitutes at the ankle as the dorsalis pedis. The tibioperoneal is patent with no evidence of stenosis. The peroneal artery is patent but small in calibre. The posterior tibial artery is patent at its origin and occludes after 3 cm. It reconstitutes behind the ankle. a) Critique the angiosome concept in chronic limb threatening ischaemia (CLTI). b) You decide to perform tibial revascularisation. Justify your choice of approach. c) Evaluate the options for antithrombotic therapy in this patient. d) Your revascularisation was initially successful and the toe was amputated. However, after 4 weeks, the revascularisation has failed and the wound edges are necrotic. Repeat imaging shows no further options for revascularisation. Describe how you will manage this patient.

questions.stem: Colleague suspected operating under the influence of alcohol
questions.verbatim: You notice one of your colleagues appears to be performing poorly whilst operating and suspect they are under the influence of alcohol. Discuss your approach to this situation.

questions.stem: Brachiocephalic AVF: central venous stenosis causes & management
questions.verbatim: A patient has a right brachiocephalic arterio-venous fistula. What may alert you to a central venous stenosis? What are the commonest causes? Discuss your management options.

questions.stem: Company rep new device: information before adopting into practice
questions.verbatim: A representative of a company approaches you regarding using a new device for the treatment for occlusive femoral disease. What information should you consider before implementing it into your practice?

questions.stem: Radiation safety in complex endovascular procedures
questions.verbatim: You are planning to perform a complex endovascular procedure. Discuss the issues related to radiation safety for the patient and the surgical team and strategies to minimise these risks.

questions.stem: Aortic intramural haematoma: pathophysiology & treatment algorithm
questions.verbatim: Define the pathophysiology of aortic intramural haematoma. Discuss your treatment algorithm for its management.

questions.stem: 60M 5.7cm AAA, visceral segment involved; experience disclosure; post-op ileus
questions.verbatim: A 60 year old taxi driver is referred for management by his GP after an abdominal ultrasound shows the presence of a 5.7 cm aortic aneurysm. a) Discuss your initial assessment and management. b) The visceral segment is involved; evaluate your management options. c) The patient asks you about your experience in aortic aneurysm repair. How would you respond? d) The patient has left iliac fossa pain and an ileus 7 days post-surgery. What are your concerns and how would you manage this?

questions.stem: CEA outcomes outside accepted range on audit; league tables debate
questions.verbatim: You have planned a carotid endarterectomy on an obese symptomatic patient with a recent TIA. You anticipate the procedure to be difficult because of a higher than usual bifurcation. Just prior to the surgery you are informed that during an audit review by the AVA, your outcomes for carotid endarterectomies are outside the accepted range and your practice will be reviewed. How would you approach and deal with this situation? Discuss the publication of performance / league tables for procedures such as carotid endarterectomy, CABG, hip replacement, Whipples, etc., and give your reasons for supporting or opposing them.

questions.stem: Dialysis fistula causing hand ischaemia (steal): options
questions.verbatim: Compare and contrast the treatment options for a dialysis fistula causing hand ischaemia.

questions.stem: Compare CTA, ultrasound, MRA, DSA for peripheral vascular disease
questions.verbatim: Compare and contrast CTA, ultrasound, MRA and DSA as imaging modalities for peripheral vascular disease.

questions.stem: 65M popliteal artery aneurysm: management algorithm
questions.verbatim: A 65 year old male felt a lump behind his knee and was confirmed to have a popliteal artery aneurysm. Outline your management algorithm of this patient and discuss your rationale.

questions.stem: 15yo excessive sweating of hands & feet (hyperhidrosis)
questions.verbatim: A mother brings her 15 year old daughter who is suffering with excessive sweating of the hands and feet to see you. Discuss your assessment and management options for this patient.

questions.stem: 30M knee dislocation, popliteal artery occlusion; revascularisation & swelling
questions.verbatim: A 30 year old male is referred after falling off a wall while intoxicated and has dislocated his knee (with significant genu recurvatum) and a long delay in obtaining help. He is referred to your trauma centre from 3 hours away. You are told he has a pale, cold, pulseless and altered sensation in the lower leg and foot. There is instability of the knee joint and boggy swelling behind the knee. 1) Discuss your plans and considerations prior to arrival. 2) Discuss your initial assessment and management and any investigations. 3) There is abrupt occlusion to flow in the above-knee popliteal artery and no contrast visible in the infragenicular vessels. Outline your operative management. 4) The patient develops significant swelling after revascularisation. How will you assess and manage?

questions.stem: Assessment of frailty & impact on vascular decision-making
questions.verbatim: “Frailty: it is hard to define but you know it when you see it”. Discuss the assessment of patient frailty and its impact on decision making in vascular surgery patients.

questions.stem: Type B aortic dissection: management algorithm & influencing factors
questions.verbatim: Discuss and justify your management algorithm for the treatment of type B aortic dissection and indicate what factors may influence your decision.

questions.stem: Radiation safety in complex endovascular procedures
questions.verbatim: You are planning to perform a complex endovascular procedure. Discuss the issues related to radiation safety for the patient and the surgical team and strategies to minimise these risks.

questions.stem: 55M chronic mesenteric ischaemia (SMA, coeliac, IMA stenosis)
questions.verbatim: While investigating a 55-year-old man for short distance claudication, an abdominal CTA reveals high grade stenosis of the SMA and coeliac artery and a significant IMA origin stenosis. What advice would you give and how would you manage this patient?

questions.stem: Defend surgical management in treatment of venous ulcer
questions.verbatim: Defend surgical management in the treatment of venous ulcer.

questions.stem: 35M gunshot infraclavicular, occluded subclavian artery; catastrophic bleeding; infection
questions.verbatim: A 35-year-old intoxicated man sustained a single gunshot to the left infra-clavicular region. A CTA of the area demonstrates a large haematoma and absent flow in the second part of the subclavian artery over 3 centimetres, with an associated fractured left clavicle. There is no ongoing bleeding from the wound. His left upper limb pulses are absent, and he is complaining of increasing left upper limb pain and hand weakness. 1. What is the initial management? 2. Evaluate the management options of the occluded subclavian artery. What is your preferred option and why? 3. You explore the wound and experience catastrophic bleeding. How will you manage this? 4. 24 hours later, you are called to see him with a large volume turbid discharge from the wound. How will you manage this?

questions.stem: Rationale for screening for carotid artery disease
questions.verbatim: Discuss the rationale for screening Carotid artery disease.

questions.stem: 35yo diabetic progressive foot deformity (Charcot)
questions.verbatim: A 35-year-old diabetic patient presents with a progressive foot deformity. Discuss the pathophysiological processes involved and how these influence management. (X-ray included).

questions.stem: 69M diabetic gangrenous toe, SFA occlusion: conduits, graft failure, surveillance
questions.verbatim: A 69-year-old diabetic gentleman presents with an infected gangrenous left great toe. He has varicose veins on his left leg. His arteriography shows a long SFA occlusion, occluded popliteal artery with reconstitution of posterior tibial artery at mid-calf level. Discuss options of conduits for bypass surgery, causes of bypass graft failure and postoperative surveillance protocol.

questions.stem: 50M ESRF thrombosed brachiocephalic fistula, recirculation
questions.verbatim: A 50-year-old diabetic ESRF patient has been dialysing through a left arm brachiocephalic fistula for 3 years. Recently, the dialysis nurse had voiced concerns about recirculation during haemodialysis. He presented to ED with a thrombosed fistula having been dialysed 3 days ago. Discuss management of this patient.

questions.stem: Handover to colleague before leave: reliable methods
questions.verbatim: You are about to hand over a patient to a colleague prior to going on leave. Outline how you would proceed with this including any recognised methods you would employ to make it more reliable and effective.

questions.stem: 65M aorto-bifemoral graft infection with groin sinus: investigations, treatment, antibiotics
questions.verbatim: A 65-year-old man who had an aorto-bifemoral bypass graft one year ago presents with a purulent discharge from a sinus in the left groin. 1. How would you assess this patient and justify the investigations you would perform? 2. Discuss the options for treatment. 3. Discuss the factors that would influence your choice of procedure. 4. Explain your rationale behind the antibiotic management for this patient.

questions.stem: Popliteal cystic adventitial disease: aetiology, investigation, treatment
questions.verbatim: Discuss the aetiology and pathophysiology of popliteal Cystic Adventitial Disease. Outline your investigations and treatment strategy with justification.

questions.stem: 28F uncontrolled HTN, bilateral renal artery stenosis (FMD)
questions.verbatim: A 28-year-old woman is referred with uncontrolled hypertension (BP 220/110). An MRA shows stenosis in both renal arteries. What is the most likely diagnosis, its pathophysiology and the management options? [Image: bilateral renal MRA — refer to original exam]

questions.stem: Approaches to first rib resection: advantages & disadvantages
questions.verbatim: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each of the different approaches to 1st rib resection.

questions.stem: Groin wound complication audit + junior staff undermining authority
questions.verbatim: You have been appointed as a new consultant in a large teaching vascular surgery unit. As part of a unit audit, a trend of increased groin wound complications has been seen in your patients. It has been made aware to you that the junior staff have been making disparaging comments about you to the other staff and undermining your authority as a result. How would you manage this?

questions.stem: Antiphospholipid syndrome in vascular patients
questions.verbatim: Write short notes on the Antiphospholipid Syndrome. How might this present and how does it influence therapy in vascular patients?

questions.stem: 77M post-CEA neck swelling (haematoma/pseudoaneurysm); later ICA occlusion
questions.verbatim: A 77-year-old male had a left carotid endarterectomy six weeks ago. A superficial wound infection was successfully treated with oral antibiotics. You are called by your registrar to the emergency department where the patient has presented with acute left neck pain and obvious neck swelling. 1. What would you discuss with your registrar? 2. Outline your differential diagnosis and outline a management plan for each. 3. The patient is otherwise fit and active and you have decided on open operative management. Clearly describe your operative management and procedure. 4. Five days after your surgery the patient develops some neurological symptoms. An ultrasound and CT angiogram show the internal carotid artery is occluded. Describe your management.

questions.stem: Chronic venous hypertension: aetiology, pathophysiology & treatment
questions.verbatim: Outline the aetiology and pathophysiology of chronic venous hypertension and how this guides your treatment of it.

questions.stem: 65F myeloproliferative disorder, mid-SFA occlusion claudication
questions.verbatim: A 65-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with a myeloproliferative disorder and has just completed a course of chemotherapy. She presents with a three-week history of disabling claudication. She is an estate agent and wants to get back to work and walk distances. A duplex ultrasound shows a 6 cm long mid-SFA occlusion with 3-vessel run-off. 1. What are her management options and what would you choose and why?

questions.stem: Medial vs posterior approach for open popliteal aneurysm repair
questions.verbatim: Compare and contrast the medial and posterior approach with regards to open popliteal artery aneurysm repair.

questions.stem: Hazards of blood transfusion; restrictive vs liberal policies
questions.verbatim: Blood transfusion is commonly lifesaving in the context of complex surgery. Regretfully however, this comes at a price. 1. What are the hazards associated with blood transfusion in surgery? Mention specific complications, both early and late, with possible causes and therapies for such where known. 2. What do you understand by the terms ‘restrictive’ and ‘liberal’ blood transfusion policies in surgery? How are these being applied in contemporary practice and what is the evidence for each?

questions.stem: Five aortic arch abnormalities with reference to embryology
questions.verbatim: Describe five abnormalities of the aortic arch with reference to its embryological development and how they may be clinically relevant.

questions.stem: 62F acute-on-chronic mesenteric ischaemia; occluded aorta/coeliac/SMA; short bowel
questions.verbatim: A 62-year-old female presents with a 4-hour history of severe abdominal pain in the setting of 6 months of post-prandial pain associated with 15 kg weight loss. 1. Discuss your initial assessment and ED management. 2. CT angiography reveals extensive atherosclerotic disease with an occluded distal aorta just below the renal arteries, with an occluded coeliac axis and a heavily calcified SMA origin with occlusion. Discuss your management algorithm. 3. The day after revascularisation, the patient remains hypotensive despite inotropes and her lactate remains elevated. What is your management plan? 4. What is the implication of extensive bowel resection? You are asked to attend a meeting with the family. How would you approach this discussion?

questions.stem: 50M painful non-healing index-finger ulcer: differential diagnosis
questions.verbatim: A GP sends you a 50-year-old male patient with a very painful, non-healing ulcer on the left index finger. What is your differential diagnosis? Discuss history, examination, and investigations you would consider important, with justification.

questions.stem: Embryology of popliteal artery & classification of entrapment
questions.verbatim: Outline the embryological development of the popliteal artery and how this relates to the classification of popliteal entrapment syndrome.

questions.stem: 30yo carpenter, effort-induced upper-extremity pain/weakness
questions.verbatim: A 30-year-old carpenter presents with unilateral effort-induced upper extremity pain and weakness. How would you assess and manage this patient?

questions.stem: Ionizing radiation effects on vascular tissue & reconstruction decisions
questions.verbatim: Outline the pathophysiological changes that ionizing radiation has on the tissue in the vascular system and how this may impact your decision regarding any vascular reconstruction.

questions.stem: Registrar research-integrity/authorship dilemma; mentoring
questions.verbatim: You are a junior consultant. A non-training registrar who is interested in a surgical career approaches you and asks for help with their research requirement for their SET application. The registrar indicates that they can write a paper from some research done by a colleague, who has said they can use the work despite the registrar not having contributed. Describe how you as a mentor would deal with this situation.

questions.stem: 26F, 20wk pregnant, iliofemoral DVT & phlegmasia; anticoagulation in pregnancy
questions.verbatim: A 26-year-old pregnant woman, currently 20 weeks gestation, presents to the emergency department with a one-day history of a swollen, painful left leg. She also complains of mild chest discomfort with shortness of breath. a) How would you further evaluate this patient? b) Discuss the pathogenesis of DVT during pregnancy and the use of anticoagulation during pregnancy. c) She has left-sided iliofemoral DVT. After 24 hours of optimal medical therapy, she deteriorates with severe pain, massive swelling, purple discoloration, and sensori-motor changes in her foot. Discuss your further management. d) After an uneventful delivery of a healthy baby, she still has a mildly swollen left leg. What will your long-term management involve?

questions.stem: Carotid duplex technique & criteria in recent stroke; ICA occlusion images
questions.verbatim: Describe how you would perform a carotid duplex scan in a patient with a recent stroke. Discuss and justify your diagnostic criteria. What images would you acquire if you believe the right ICA is occluded?

questions.stem: Giant Cell Arteritis: vascular surgeon's role in diagnosis & management
questions.verbatim: Discuss the condition Giant Cell Arteritis and the role a vascular surgeon might play in its diagnosis and management.

questions.stem: Spinal cord ischaemia with aortic procedures: pathophysiology & rescue
questions.verbatim: Discuss the pathophysiology of Spinal Cord Ischaemia (SCI) associated with aortic procedures. Explain the rationale for therapies to mitigate or rescue SCI.

questions.stem: Type II endoleak with sac expansion 2y after EVAR
questions.verbatim: Discuss your assessment and management options for a patient with a type 2 endoleak and aneurysm sac expansion 2 years following endovascular stent graft repair of a AAA.

questions.stem: Informed consent for an indigenous patient; cultural safety
questions.verbatim: You are consenting a female patient who has identified culturally and tribally as an indigenous person of the country in which you are consulting. This is for a significant and medically indicated operation. Without making eye contact the patient agrees that she understands your explanation and will sign. How do you ensure informed consent is taking place for this patient?

questions.stem: 85M 5.5cm distal arch/proximal descending aneurysm involving LSA
questions.verbatim: An 85-year-old male presents with uncontrolled hypertension, retrosternal chest and left shoulder pain on a background of a known 5.5 cm distal arch and proximal descending aortic aneurysm involving the left subclavian artery origin. Discuss your clinical approach to this patient, including potential management and treatment options.

questions.stem: 48M progressive short-distance claudication: assessment & investigations
questions.verbatim: A 48-year-old tradesman presents with a history of progressive short-distance claudication. Describe your initial assessment, possible diagnoses and relevant investigations.

questions.stem: 58M carotid disease with planned CABG: combined management
questions.verbatim: A cardiac surgeon contacts you regarding a 58-year-old man for whom coronary artery bypass is planned. The patient is known to have carotid disease, and the cardiac surgeon would like your assessment and advice on how this should be managed in relation to the coronary artery bypass. Compare treatment options available and explain how different factors would be important in your decision making.

questions.stem: 24F popliteal/gastrocnemius DVT; post-thrombotic syndrome
questions.verbatim: A 24-year-old woman is referred for your advice 3 months following presentation with unilateral leg swelling and a duplex ultrasound reporting gastrocnemius and popliteal vein DVT. She has been treated initially with Clexane followed by a DOAC (Direct Oral Anticoagulant). She is concerned by her leg swelling. Discuss the clinical features, pathophysiology and risk factors contributing to the development of Post-Thrombotic Syndrome. Discuss the natural history and treatment options that you would discuss including the potential benefits.

questions.stem: Persistent sciatic artery with reference to limb arterial embryology
questions.verbatim: Discuss Persistent Sciatic Artery with reference to the embryological development of the lower limb arterial circulation. Describe the anatomical and clinical hallmarks of this condition.

questions.stem: ESRF: options for renal replacement, pros & cons of each
questions.verbatim: List all the options a patient with end-stage renal failure may have for renal replacement. Describe the pros and cons of each option.

questions.stem: Radiation-induced vs atherosclerotic carotid stenosis
questions.verbatim: Compare the pathogenesis and management of radiation-induced versus atherosclerotic carotid stenosis.

questions.stem: Short notes: management of blunt thoracic aortic injury
questions.verbatim: Write short notes on management of Blunt Thoracic Aortic Injury.

questions.stem: 59F saccular 1cm common iliac outpouching (?mycotic/saccular aneurysm)
questions.verbatim: A 59-year-old female presents to ED with moderate central abdominal pain and a low-grade fever. A CT scan shows a saccular 1 cm outpouching from the lateral aspect of the right common iliac artery origin and an otherwise normal calibre infrarenal aorta with scattered non-stenotic calcific disease. Discuss your differential diagnosis, relevant history, examination and investigations, and possible management options.

questions.stem: Pathophysiology of ischaemia-reperfusion injury (IRI)
questions.verbatim: Describe the pathophysiology involved with ischaemia – reperfusion injury (IRI).

questions.stem: 9yo supracondylar fracture, pulseless hand: management algorithm
questions.verbatim: An orthopaedic surgeon calls you to their theatre. A 9-year-old child has sustained a supracondylar fracture. The patient is on the table under general anaesthetic. The fracture has been reduced. The hand has no palpable pulses. Discuss the important issues and describe your management algorithm.

questions.stem: Compare & contrast endovenous interventions for varicose veins
questions.verbatim: Compare and contrast endovenous interventions for varicose veins.

questions.stem: 55M diabetic plantar ulcer & hammer toes: diagnosis, classification, treatment
questions.verbatim: You are asked to see a 55-year-old diabetic male with obvious hammer toes and chronic nail changes who has a non-healing mid-foot plantar ulcer. His foot is pictured below. [Image: clinical photograph of the patient’s foot — please refer to the original exam for the photograph] What is the most likely diagnosis? Discuss the epidemiology, pathogenesis and classification of this condition. Describe how you would treat this plantar ulcer and discuss the rationale of your approach.

questions.stem: Renal fibromuscular dysplasia: pathophysiology & presentation
questions.verbatim: Discuss the pathophysiology and clinical presentation of renal Fibromuscular Dysplasia.

questions.stem: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT): diagnosis & management
questions.verbatim: Discuss the pathophysiology, diagnosis and management of Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT), including how this would influence future vascular interventions.

questions.stem: Management of a stab wound to Zone 2 of the neck
questions.verbatim: How would you manage a stab wound to Zone 2 of the neck?

questions.stem: Designing an effective Morbidity & Mortality (M&M) meeting format
questions.verbatim: You have been tasked with developing a new departmental morbidity and mortality (M & M) meeting format. a) Outline the principles of an effective Morbidity and Mortality meeting. Include in your answer the definition of M & M meetings. b) Describe the challenges to the ideal conduct of M & M meetings.

questions.stem: 50M left leg swelling, non-thrombotic iliac vein lesion: stenting technique; thrombus on completion venogram; expanding thigh haematoma after sheath removal
questions.verbatim: An otherwise well 50-year-old man presents with left leg swelling and imaging suggesting compression at the left common iliac vein consistent with a non-thrombotic iliac vein lesion. a) Describe how you perform stenting to treat this condition. b) You perform a completion venogram and find thrombus at the distal end of the stent. What is your management? c) At the end of the procedure, you remove the sheath from the thigh and note a very large, expanding haematoma in the thigh. What would you do now?
